cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T3's stop-everything plan directly: a reset gives no data.
cells.limitation: T6 and T8 ignore the turn before; T8 restates T2's let-alone stance.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T7 adds falsification framing: stopping all never tests whether one product is safe.
cells.limitation: T9 repeats T3 nearly verbatim; no distinction is introduced after T4.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T5 sets comfort against data: data is a poor consolation for stinging.
cells.limitation: Irritation versus allergy, actives, or interaction between products never raised by any mind.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 merges recovery with one-at-a-time reintroduction from T3 and T4.
cells.limitation: T10 Skeptic simply agrees; Minimalist's position never reshapes or gets reshaped.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section E lands on stop all, reach baseline, reintroduce one by one.
cells.limitation: Same plan was in T3; Section D calls settled point still disputed.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 accurately notes that stopping alone is a reset, not a test.
cells.limitation: T4 and T7 treat T3 as stop-only, though T3 included one-at-a-time reintroduction.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T5 challenges the cost of experimentation against the user's comfort.
cells.limitation: T7's objection rests on misreading T3; target never answers it, only restates.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T2, T5, T8 Walden lines match Thoreau's text as remembered.
cells.limitation: T4 implies continuing products on stinging skin; T7 claims stopping all yields no knowledge.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section E conditions advice on severity rather than asserting one path.
cells.limitation: T10 calls it the only logical way; T3 asserts the system is failing.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T10 Skeptic accepts T9's baseline-first sequence.
cells.limitation: T10 concession names no cause; Minimalist never answers T7's identification objection.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A frames finding the irritant versus healing quickly.
cells.limitation: Whether stinging is expected adjustment, irritation or allergy is never distinguished.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 uses the three new products as three variables, one result.
cells.limitation: Timing of last week and product types never shape the argument.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T1 and T10 address the user's stated goal of finding the cause.
cells.limitation: T2 and T8 push Minimalist's let-alone value over the user's diagnostic goal.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: Section E separates severe from mild irritation.
cells.limitation: No mention of swelling, hives or when to see a clinician; stakes stay vague.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on severity of the irritation.
cells.limitation: Never asks which products or ingredients, or if any are acids or retinoids.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section A names a desire to restore skin quickly.
cells.limitation: No alternative motives offered; why the user chose three products never explored.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T7 questions the assumption that untested products are safe.
cells.limitation: Assumption that a single product is the culprit, not a combination, goes unexamined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section D names data versus relief as the competing priorities.
cells.limitation: User is never invited to weigh knowing the culprit against simplifying the routine.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T5 acknowledges the discomfort of a stinging face.
cells.limitation: No fear, worry about damage, or pressure behind the new routine is touched.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E lets the user place themselves on severity.
cells.limitation: No question or distinction offered for the user to accept or refine.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: T3, T4, T8 lay out stop-and-reintroduce, test while continuing, and simplify.
cells.limitation: Patch testing and seeing a dermatologist are never listed as options.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T5 weighs data gained against continued discomfort.
cells.limitation: Time cost of serial reintroduction and loss of product benefits never stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E splits on severe versus mild irritation.
cells.limitation: Both branches stop all products; no observable sign defines severe.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T7 notes the user remains in the dark about the irritant.
cells.limitation: Consequential unknowns (allergy, actives, interactions) never separated from minor ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: Section E: stop, wait for baseline, reintroduce one by one, days apart.
cells.limitation: No patch-test step or point at which to seek medical help.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T3 and T9 state the plan in plain steps.
cells.limitation: T7's falsify the hypothesis phrasing adds abstraction to a simple point.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T10's that clearly refers to T9's sequence.
cells.limitation: T5 and T6 you could mean the user or another mind; addressee unclear.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, quick to read.
cells.limitation: T1, T2, T3, T6 fall under 25 words.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Minimalist's Walden lines in T2, T5, T8 mark a distinct voice.
cells.limitation: Skeptic and Efficiency Expert converge on one plan by T10 in similar register.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns stay brief without long recaps.
cells.limitation: T9 repeats T3; T10 repeats T4; Section D restates Section A.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T5 contrasts a stinging face with abstract data.
cells.limitation: Tension stays low; skin harm stakes never made concrete.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T10 Skeptic moves to the baseline-first plan.
cells.limitation: T10 reversal names no argument that changed the Skeptic's mind.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T8 Minimalist: let the skin breathe, with Thoreau's let-alone line.
cells.limitation: Efficiency Expert in T3, T6, T9 speaks in generic system jargon.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T6: your routine is a liability, not a habit.
cells.limitation: Memorable lines are borrowed Walden quotations; no analogy built for skincare.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T5 brief emotional turn toward the user's discomfort.
cells.limitation: Flat rhythm throughout; no build toward the T10 convergence.

strengths: Section E gives a standard, usable plan: stop all, reach baseline, reintroduce one at a time.
Minimalist's Walden lines in T2, T5, T8 give one distinct, recognisable voice.
T5 names the real tension between relief from stinging and diagnostic data.
weaknesses: No mind asks which products or ingredients, or flags allergy signs needing medical care.
T4 and T7 misread T3's plan as stop-only, so the main disagreement is illusory.
T10 Skeptic agrees with no stated cause; T9 and T10 repeat T3 and T4.

symptoms.observed: Never asks which products or ingredients, though that decides the testing order.
symptoms.evidence: You have three variables and one result.

symptoms.observed: Skeptic treats T3's stop-then-reintroduce plan as stopping only.
symptoms.evidence: If you stop all, you never falsify the hypothesis

symptoms.observed: Skeptic converges on T9's plan without naming what changed his mind.
symptoms.evidence: That is the only logical way to gain knowledge.

symptoms.observed: No turn or section mentions allergy warning signs or seeing a clinician.
symptoms.evidence: If the skin irritation is severe, stop all products immediately

symptoms.observed: T9 repeats T3's plan; no new distinction after T4.
symptoms.evidence: stop all, wait for the baseline, then introduce one at a time

findings.description: Four turns fall under 25 words, per deterministic checks.
T4 implies keeping products in use on stinging skin while testing; T7 claims stopping all yields no knowledge, though T3 included reintroduction.
No mention of allergic-reaction signs (swelling, hives, blistering) or when to seek medical care.
Calls it disputed whether data is worth continued irritation, though the agreed plan involves no continued irritation.
Walden lines in pd=true turns appear close to Thoreau's text from memory; not checked against a source.

rubric_fit_notes: A practical troubleshooting question gives criterion 4 little natural material; low C4 ratings reflect missed openings (why three products at once, worry about damage) rather than rubric mismatch. Popper and Clear fit the topic loosely.
raw.question_type_note: Read as a decision: choosing a troubleshooting procedure, so C5 rewarded the stop-and-reintroduce plan and penalised missing thresholds and medical-care branch.
